title: Git still has the work you just deleted
topic: getting deleted commits back with git reflog

alternates: You just wiped three days of commits. Git still has them.
hook.headline: 3 DAYS OF WORK, GONE?

params.title: my-app
lines: HEAD is now at 4f2a9c1 login page

story.promise: the three lost days of work come back

facts.claim: A branch in Git is a lightweight movable pointer to a commit
git reset --hard discards changes and moves the branch back to an earlier commit
Reflogs record when the tips of branches were updated in the local repository
Reflog entries are kept for 90 days by default before git gc may expire them

beats.narration: A hard reset moved your branch back three commits, and git log can't see them.
beats.headline: MAIN DROPPED FROM 9 TO 6

story.after: the tower drops to 6 COMMITS: GIT LOG SHOWS 6
story.action: three blocks fall off the top of the tower

beats.narration: But git prints a receipt every time your branch moves. It's called the reflog.
beats.headline: 1 RECEIPT PER BRANCH MOVE

story.before: the lost commits look gone for good
story.after: 10 receipts piled up in the REFLOG
story.action: receipts print and drop onto the pile, one per move

beats.narration: Run git reflog, and your lost commit sits one line down.
beats.headline: GIT REFLOG: C13F8AA

story.after: c13f8aa on the reflog: LOST COMMIT FOUND
story.action: the host types git reflog and the lost commit appears one line down

beats.narration: Those receipts last ninety days by default, so you have time.
beats.headline: KEPT FOR 90 DAYS

story.after: the c13f8aa receipt shows 88 days left: KEPT FOR 90 DAYS
story.action: the days counter ticks down slowly from 90

beats.narration: Reset back to that line, and all three days of work come home.
beats.headline: RESET --HARD C13F8AA

story.before: main at 6 commits, c13f8aa only in the reflog
story.after: c13f8aa back on top of git log: 9 COMMITS BACK HOME
story.action: the host throws c13f8aa into the terminal and the log refills

cta.narration: Comment GIT and I'll send you the rescue commands.

premises: A tower of 9 save-point blocks: a reset knocks the top 3 off, they are found in a lost-and-found bin, and stacked back on.

One commit, c13f8aa, that holds three days of work: a hard reset hides it, but git printed a receipt when the branch moved, the reflog lists it, the receipt is good for 90 days, and resetting to it brings the work home.
A detective follows footprints (branch moves) through the repository until they lead to the missing commit.
story.why: A single commit id is something the viewer can carry and read on every screen; it disappears from git log, shows up on a receipt, and ends as the branch tip again.
story.object: commit c13f8aa, three days of work
story.spine: You reset and three days of commits vanish from git log. But git printed a receipt every time the branch moved. Therefore git reflog shows c13f8aa one line down, and the receipt lasts 90 days. Until finally a reset back to it brings all 9 commits home.
story.ending: git log shows all 9 commits again with c13f8aa on top: 9 COMMITS BACK HOME.
